validity.recommendation: No action on existence/classification/duplicate. This is a real, extensively and independently documented proposed international project -- not a GEM-only fabrication and not a duplicate of any other row on the 32-pipeline Far East roster (it is the only entry that is a Russia-DPRK-ROK international transit line; P0758/P2027 and the rest of the SKV family are wholly domestic Russian trunk infrastructure that would merely feed gas TOWARD this proposed line's Vladivostok origin, a genuinely distinct relationship, not an identity). Fuel=Gas and PipelineType=transmission are both uncontested.
validity.researcher_notes: Checked existence against 6 independent outlets across the whole 1991-2022 span: Reuters (2018-06-29, Wayback), UPI/Yonhap-sourced reporting (2018-10-25, Wayback), Hankyoreh/hani.co.kr (2018-10-24, Korean-language, hand-confirmed), The Diplomat (2019-01-09 and 2022-04), and CSIS's 'Pipe Dreams to Pipelines' analysis (~2015). All six describe the same project: a Gazprom/KOGAS(-and-implicitly-North Korea) plan for a Russia-to-South-Korea gas pipeline transiting North Korea, originating from Russia's Far East (Vladivostok / the Sakhalin-Khabarovsk-Vladivostok system) and connecting to KOGAS's South Korean grid. Checked against the batch's 32-row Far East roster: no other row describes an international DPRK/ROK-transiting line, so this is not a relabeled duplicate of any domestic Russian segment. oilprice.com serves the CSIS piece verbatim on one URL (not independent of CSIS) but ALSO carries a second, genuinely separate original article by Tsvetana Paraskova ('Is The Russia-Korea Pipeline Feasible?') -- treated as a distinct independent source, not double-counted with CSIS.

validity.recommendation: Do NOT fill EndState/Province as 'South Gyeongsang' to match the merged route geometry as originally scoped -- the geometry itself appears to be the error. The North Korean midpoint (~40.87 deg N, 127.70 deg E) also doesn't align well with Wonsan (~39.15 deg N). RouteAccuracy for this geometry should NOT be presumed reliable; flagging it as a route candidate for a human §8 correction rather than auto-replacing it (per hard requirement: a route is never auto-replaced). Filled EndLocation/EndState per the SOURCED value (Pyeongtaek / Gyeonggi Province) rather than the geometry's actual endpoint, consistent with the batch's 'judge the route first' rule.

Genuine source conflict, not a gap -- three non-agreeing construction-cost-adjacent figures were found and NONE was forced into the field: (1) The Diplomat (2019): 'the cost of pipeline laying would be about $2.5 billion.' (2) CSIS (~2015): 'Initial estimates suggested that the 12 bcma pipeline would cost around $6.3 billion.' These two do not agree and appear to be different-vintage estimates for different route/capacity assumptions, not a rounding difference. (3) UPI (2018, Wayback): a SEPARATE and different metric entirely -- a projected North Korea TRANSIT FEE (not construction cost) of '$158 million... annually' (article headline rounds this to '$195M'), per a KOGAS/KGC estimate reported via Yonhap, calculated by analogy to Gazprom's Ukraine/Belarus/Slovakia transit contracts. This transit-fee figure must not be conflated with SegmentCost (construction cost) -- it is excluded here on that basis, not merely because it's unsourced. Given the genuine $2.5B-vs-$6.3B disagreement between the two real construction-cost candidates, and no way to determine which (if either) GEM intends, leaving UNRESOLVED with both documented rather than picking one.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Newest PROJECT-SPECIFIC dated evidence found is The Diplomat's 2019-01-09 piece (Reuters 2018-06-29 is slightly older). A 6th wiki-cited source (rg.ru, 'V Seule obsudili prokladku gazoprovoda iz Rossii v Iuzhnuiu Koreiu,' dated 2019-06-28, which would be the single newest citation on GEM's own page) could NOT be verified as of this audit: rg.ru returned HTTP 401 direct (likely a post-2022 geo-block on a Russian state outlet, not evidence of deletion), the cited Google cache URL is dead (Google retired web-cache serving; returns a bare Google-search redirect stub, no article content), and the Wayback CDX API returned 'Internet Archive: Temporarily Offline' on repeated attempts across this session -- an infrastructure outage, not a content finding. Not used as a citation; not treated as resolving the status question either way. The Diplomat's 2022-04 piece discusses the same Russia-DPRK-ROK pipeline concept generically ('prior South Korean administrations have considered') without naming this specific project, past-tense-framed -- consistent with, but not independent proof of, continued dormancy through April 2022. No project-specific news of any kind (resumed talks, formal cancellation, revived interest) was found for 2020-2026 in any source reached (CSIS, OilPrice, both Diplomat pieces, WebSearch). Applying the batch's dormancy-inference rule: a project already recorded 'shelved' with no confirmable project-specific evidence more recent than 2019 is well past the '>=4y dormant -> cancelled' threshold as of 2026-09-14 (roughly 7-7.5 years since the newest confirmable evidence). Proposing Status=cancelled with ShelvedCancelledType=inferred (lowercase per controlled vocab), per rule 2 with NO fabricated confirming URL for the cancellation itself -- this is a mechanical dormancy inference, not a sourced fact, and should be labeled as such. Important caveat for whoever applies this: unlike a typical shelved commercial project, this pipeline's dormancy is structurally tied to unresolved North Korea sanctions/political-risk conditions and has already had multiple historical proposal/dormancy cycles (1991, 2008, 2011) -- a future thaw in inter-Korean or Russia-DPRK relations could plausibly revive it under a different administration, so 'inferred cancelled' should be understood as 'no active current initiative found,' not as a claim that the underlying strategic rationale has been abandoned by any party.
